item.title: C/C++ 'extern inline' Semantics Explained: Header vs. Source File Usage
item.description:
“C/C++ ’extern inline’ Semantics Explained: Header vs. Source File Usage”

What precisely dictates the behavior and linkage requirements when employing the inline function specifier in C or C++, especially when contrasted with using extern inline within header and source files? Exploring the subtle differences reveals key aspects of translation unit visibility and optimization preferences.

Primary Function of extern inline

The central utility of declaring a function as extern inline is to explicitly inform the compiler about which object file is expected to retain the visible, externally accessible definition of the generated code.

item.title: C++ Expression Evaluation Order vs Precedence and Associativity Explained
item.description:
“C++ Expression Evaluation Order vs Precedence and Associativity Explained”

A core concept in C and C++ programming revolves around how expressions are evaluated. There’s a persistent belief, often fueled by documentation from specific platforms like MSDN regarding their particular implementations, that operator precedence and associativity dictate the precise order in which operands are evaluated. This thread seeks clarification on this relationship, particularly concerning sequence points and side effects.

Is Operator Precedence Deterministic for Operand Evaluation Order?

The central inquiry is whether operator precedence forces a specific order for operand evaluation. The general consensus among expert observations suggests that no, precedence does not determine the order of operand evaluation.
